audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Kings / Melakhim Bet Hezekiah reform, Assyrian conquest, tribute, Jerusalem delegation, and Rabshakeh propaganda narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for centralized religious reform, bronze-serpent destruction, Philistine campaign, Samaria deportation recap, Sennacherib's conquest of Judah, temple stripping for tribute, siege delegation, multilingual propaganda, bodily humiliation threats, deceptive resettlement promises, and civilian silence.

verses.restored: In third year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel, Hezekiah son of Ahaz king of Judah became king.

familiar.text: Now it came to pass in the third year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel, that Hezekiah the son of Ahaz king of Judah began to reign.

verses.restored: Twenty-five years old was he when he became king, and twenty-nine years he reigned in Jerusalem. Name of his mother was Abi daughter of Zechariah.

familiar.text: Twenty and five years old was he when he began to reign; and he reigned twenty and nine years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name also was Abi, the daughter of Zachariah.

verses.restored: He did what was right in eyes of YHWH, according to all David his father had done.

familiar.text: And he did that which was right in the sight of the LORD, according to all that David his father did.

verses.restored: He removed high places, broke pillars, cut down Asherah, and shattered bronze serpent Moses had made, for until those days children of Israel burned incense to it; he called it Nehushtan, a bronze thing.

familiar.text: He removed the high places, and brake the images, and cut down the groves, and brake in pieces the brasen serpent that Moses had made: for unto those days the children of Israel did burn incense to it: and he called it Nehushtan.

verses.restored: In YHWH Divine of Israel he trusted; after him there was none like him among all kings of Judah, nor among those before him.

familiar.text: He trusted in the LORD God of Israel; so that after him was none like him among all the kings of Judah, nor any that were before him.

verses.restored: He clung to YHWH and did not turn from following him, but kept commandments YHWH commanded Moses.

familiar.text: For he clave to the LORD, and departed not from following him, but kept his commandments, which the LORD commanded Moses.

verses.restored: YHWH was with him; wherever he went he acted wisely/prospered. He rebelled against king of Assyria and did not serve him.

familiar.text: And the LORD was with him; and he prospered whithersoever he went forth: and he rebelled against the king of Assyria, and served him not.

verses.restored: He struck Philistines as far as Gaza and its borders, from watchtower to fortified city.

familiar.text: He smote the Philistines, even unto Gaza, and the borders thereof, from the tower of the watchmen to the fenced city.

verses.restored: In fourth year of king Hezekiah, seventh year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel, Shalmaneser king of Assyria went up against Samaria and besieged it.

familiar.text: And it came to pass in the fourth year of king Hezekiah, which was the seventh year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel, that Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against Samaria, and besieged it.

verses.restored: At end of three years they captured it. In sixth year of Hezekiah, ninth year of Hoshea king of Israel, Samaria was captured.

familiar.text: And at the end of three years they took it: even in the sixth year of Hezekiah, that is the ninth year of Hoshea king of Israel, Samaria was taken.

familiar.text: And the king of Assyria did carry away Israel unto Assyria, and put them in Halah and in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes:

familiar.text: Because they obeyed not the voice of the LORD their God, but transgressed his covenant, and all that Moses the servant of the LORD commanded, and would not hear them, nor do them.

familiar.text: Now in the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah did Sennacherib king of Assyria come up against all the fenced cities of Judah, and took them.

familiar.text: At that time did Hezekiah cut off the gold from the doors of the temple of the LORD, and from the pillars which Hezekiah king of Judah had overlaid, and gave it to the king of Assyria.

familiar.text: And Rabshakeh said unto them, Speak ye now to Hezekiah, Thus saith the great king, the king of Assyria, What confidence is this wherein thou trustest?

familiar.text: Thou sayest, (but they are but vain words,) I have counsel and strength for the war. Now on whom dost thou trust, that thou rebellest against me?

familiar.text: Now, behold, thou trustest upon the staff of this bruised reed, even upon Egypt, on which if a man lean, it will go into his hand, and pierce it: so is Pharaoh king of Egypt unto all that trust on him.

verses.restored: But if you say to me, In YHWH our Divine we trust—is he not the one whose high places and altars Hezekiah removed, saying to Judah and Jerusalem, Before this altar in Jerusalem you shall bow?

familiar.text: But if ye say unto me, We trust in the LORD our God: is not that he, whose high places and whose altars Hezekiah hath taken away, and hath said to Judah and Jerusalem, Ye shall worship before this altar in Jerusalem?

familiar.text: How then wilt thou turn away the face of one captain of the least of my master’s servants, and put thy trust on Egypt for chariots and for horsemen?

familiar.text: Am I now come up without the LORD against this place to destroy it? The LORD said to me, Go up against this land, and destroy it.

verses.restored: Rabshakeh said to them, Has my lord sent me to your lord and to you to speak these words? Is it not to men sitting upon wall, who will eat their own excrement and drink their own urine with you?

familiar.text: But Rabshakeh said unto them, Hath my master sent me to thy master, and to thee, to speak these words? hath he not sent me to the men which sit on the wall, that they may eat their own dung, and drink their own piss with you?

verses.restored: Have gods of nations delivered, each his land, from hand of king of Assyria?

familiar.text: Hath any of the gods of the nations delivered at all his land out of the hand of the king of Assyria?

familiar.text: Where are the gods of Hamath, and of Arpad? where are the gods of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivah? have they delivered Samaria out of mine hand?

translation_notes: Hezekiah's reform includes destruction of local shrines and a revered bronze object. Reform may challenge exploitative institutions, but this text cannot authorize attacks on living religious communities or cultural heritage.
The bronze serpent is reduced to 'a bronze thing' because an old liberation symbol has become an object of cult. The critique concerns how symbols function, not a blanket ban on sacred art.
Hezekiah's campaign against Philistine cities and rebellion against Assyria remain military and imperial actions; positive royal evaluation does not erase conquered civilians.
The recap of Samaria's fall uses covenant theology but must preserve Assyria's siege and deportation as imperial violence.
Sennacherib captures Judah's fortified cities before Jerusalem's crisis. The displaced, killed, taxed, and besieged population extends far beyond the capital narrative.
Hezekiah strips temple doors and treasury to pay tribute. Sacred wealth cannot guarantee security, and rulers may transfer communal resources under coercion.
Rabshakeh uses accurate critique, exaggeration, humiliation, religious claims, bodily terror, economic promise, and public-language strategy as siege propaganda.
The threat of eating excrement and drinking urine describes siege starvation and is intended to terrify civilians. It must not be sensationalized or used as degrading humor.
Assyria's promise of vines, cisterns, and a similar land disguises forced deportation as benevolent relocation.
Rabshakeh claims YHWH authorized the invasion. Claims of Divine military permission require moral scrutiny and may never be treated as self-authenticating.
The people's silence is disciplined crisis response under royal command, not consent or proof that they were unafraid.
safety_note: Do not use Hezekiah's reform to justify religious vandalism, erase Philistine civilians, blame Samarian exiles, celebrate temple stripping, or imitate siege propaganda. Center civilians hearing threats in their own language, communities already conquered, and the difference between promised relocation and forced deportation.
